The I/O engine is fixed to windowsaio: on Windows it is the only one that supports direct=1.\nSynchronous engines (psync / sync) can only use buffered I/O, which measures the system cache rather than the disk, so they are not offered.

On Linux, direct=1 goes through O_DIRECT, which libaio / io_uring / psync all support.
libaio is preferred by default: only an asynchronous engine makes iodepth really take effect,
and the Q8T1 / Q32T1 performance items can only be measured accurately with it.
If this fio was not built with libaio, it falls back to an available engine at startup.
